metadata.description: Modular question bank for AI Readiness Assessment — updated for the 2025/2026 AI landscape

sections.title: AI Strategy & Vision
sections.description: Assess your organization's strategic approach to AI adoption and governance

questions.question: Our organization has a clear, documented AI strategy that connects to specific business objectives.
questions.helpText: A clear AI strategy aligns initiatives with business goals and prevents scattered adoption

questions.question: We have identified concrete use cases where AI — including generative AI and AI agents — can drive measurable outcomes (e.g., cost reduction, revenue growth, quality improvement).
Senior leaders actively champion AI initiatives by setting goals, allocating resources, and removing barriers.
We have dedicated budget and staffing for AI initiatives, including tools, training, and implementation.
Our organization has an AI governance framework that addresses ethics, responsible use, and risk management.
What is your biggest strategic challenge or opportunity when it comes to AI adoption?
questions.placeholder: e.g., Unclear ROI expectations, lack of AI governance, exciting generative AI possibilities

sections.title: Operational Readiness
sections.description: Evaluate how well your operations can integrate AI-powered solutions

questions.question: We have documented and mapped our key business processes to identify high-impact AI integration points.
We have identified tasks suitable for AI augmentation — including content generation, summarization, data analysis, and decision support.
Our operational teams are trained to work alongside AI tools and are receptive to AI-enabled process changes.
Which operational area would benefit most from AI enhancement?
What specific operational processes or tasks would you most like to improve with AI? (Optional)
questions.placeholder: e.g., Report generation, customer inquiry routing, document summarization, data entry

sections.title: Technology Infrastructure
sections.description: Assess your technical readiness for AI deployment and integration

questions.question: Our IT infrastructure supports AI workloads including API integrations with AI platforms, LLM providers, and cloud AI services.
We have experience deploying and managing cloud-based AI services, SaaS AI tools, or AI-enabled applications.
Our systems support secure data flows to and from AI services with proper access controls and audit trails.
We have established criteria for evaluating, selecting, and governing AI tools — including data residency, model transparency, and vendor risk.
What are your biggest technology concerns or gaps when it comes to implementing AI?
questions.placeholder: e.g., AI vendor lock-in, data security with LLMs, integration with legacy systems, lack of AI ops expertise

sections.title: Data Quality & Governance
sections.description: Evaluate your data readiness for AI applications and model integration

questions.question: We have high-quality, well-structured data that can be used to provide context to AI models (e.g., for RAG, fine-tuning, or analytics).
Our data is well-organized and accessible for use in AI applications, with appropriate permissions and search capabilities.
We have data governance policies that address AI-specific concerns — including training data rights, model outputs, and intellectual property.
We have clear data privacy frameworks that cover AI data processing and comply with current regulations (e.g., GDPR, state privacy laws, industry standards).
What is your biggest data challenge for AI implementation?
options: Unclear data rights for AI training and processing
Privacy, security, and compliance concerns with AI
Limited ability to prepare data for AI consumption (e.g., RAG, embeddings)
Inadequate data infrastructure for AI workloads

sections.title: Organizational Culture
sections.description: Assess cultural readiness for AI adoption and workforce transformation

questions.question: Our employees actively use AI tools in their daily work and are open to expanding AI adoption across the organization.
Teams adapt quickly to new AI capabilities, share best practices, and embrace AI-driven changes to their workflows.
Our organization invests in AI literacy training and skill development for employees at all levels.
Technical and business teams collaborate effectively to identify high-value AI opportunities and bring solutions to production.
What do you see as the biggest cultural opportunity or barrier to AI adoption in your organization?
questions.placeholder: e.g., Employees excited to learn AI tools, concerns about job displacement, need for change management

sections.title: AI-Powered Automation
sections.description: Evaluate current AI automation capabilities and opportunities

questions.question: We have implemented AI-powered automation beyond basic rule-based workflows (e.g., intelligent document processing, AI assistants, or agent workflows).
Our employees understand how AI augments their work and can proactively identify new automation opportunities.
We have hands-on experience with modern AI automation tools — such as AI coding assistants, AI agents, or AI-integrated business platforms.
We track and demonstrate ROI from AI-powered automation initiatives with clear metrics (time saved, error reduction, cost impact).
What would be your ideal next AI automation project or use case?
questions.placeholder: e.g., AI-powered customer support, automated report generation, intelligent document review, AI coding assistant
